title: UE Render Debug Capture
description: Capture rendering debug views, collect Niagara AsyncGpuTrace runtime evidence, and analyze retained DRED/render failure logs offline with explicit evidence boundaries.

recipes.title: Analyze retained rendering failure evidence
recipes.description: Read explicit finalized log and CrashContext paths locally, retaining bounded source evidence without requiring an Editor connection.

inputs.name: projectRoot
inputs.description: Absolute directory containing the retained diagnostic files.

inputs.name: files
inputs.description: One to eight explicit paths relative to projectRoot.

steps.purpose: Load the local operation schema and select finalized artifacts with explicit bounds.
Execute once through localProject; no Editor connection is needed.
Inspect the returned ranges, hashes and truncation flags. Keep each source independent and the root cause unproven; do not re-execute just to verify the response.

result.summary: Bounded DRED, device-removal, resource and queue evidence with exact source ranges.
success: metadata-only dumps are not described as decoded
active breadcrumbs and nearby resources are not treated as root causes

recipes.title: Observe a Niagara AsyncGpuTrace dispatch
recipes.description: Select a loaded world and Data Interface, then capture one bounded GPU readback with provider and frame context.

inputs.name: world
inputs.description: Exact loaded Editor or PIE world path.

inputs.name: dataInterface
inputs.description: Exact loaded AsyncGpuTrace Data Interface path.

steps.purpose: Discover loaded objects and bridge version; obtain current sessionId and generation from scene.pie.status when targeting PIE.
Capture one matching dispatch using an explicit world, DI, timeout and result limit.
Inspect the returned state and sample semantics. Only complete proves readback; do not re-execute just to verify the response.

result.summary: One observed DI dispatch aggregated across instances, with bounded result slots and provider setup context.
success: state is complete before counts are used
missing evidence remains unavailable or null
query high-water mark is not called an issued-ray count
TLAS reference presence is not claimed as lifetime proof

recipes.title: Capture and compare one rendering debug view
recipes.description: Resolve a live visualization mode, capture one exact viewport with restoration evidence, analyze it, and compare it with a compatible baseline when supplied.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Exact Editor Level Viewport or PIE session and generation target.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Visualization mode ID returned by live mode discovery.

inputs.name: baselineCaptureId
inputs.description: Compatible persisted capture used for an optional pixel comparison.

steps.purpose: Resolve live mode availability from the current Engine, RHI, optional modules, and exact viewport target.
Temporarily apply the selected mode, capture only the exact viewport, and restore the original view state on every exit path.
Read bounded mode-aware pixel, luminance, coverage, histogram, and regional evidence from the persisted capture.
When a baseline exists, verify render-fingerprint compatibility and produce bounded changed-pixel and diff-image evidence.

result.summary: Exact viewport debug-view evidence with restoration, bounded analysis, and optional compatible visual diff.
evidence: target viewport and PIE generation identity
lossless capture ID, image hash, and render fingerprint
comparison compatibility, changed-pixel ratio, and diff capture ID
success: the selected mode was reported available for the exact target
the capture came from the requested viewport rather than a desktop or unrelated window
original view mode, flags, camera, exposure, selection, and transform were restored
analysis remained bounded and did not claim raw GBuffer or RDG texture values
incompatible fingerprints produced an inconclusive comparison

resources.description: Niagara runtime capture and offline render failure contracts, optional engine bridge installation and verification limits.
Visualization availability, viewport targeting, state restoration, image-format, and analysis boundaries.
